City of Toronto: two land transfer taxes. The municipal tax adds about $16,475 on a $1,000,000 purchase, on top of the provincial tax. Estimate yours →

Overview

North York was its own city until it became part of Toronto in 1998. Today it covers much of the city's north end, from established family neighbourhoods to one of the busiest condo corridors in the GTA along Yonge Street.

Housing & pockets

High-rise condos cluster around North York Centre, Sheppard-Yonge and Finch. A few blocks off Yonge, many streets have original post-war bungalows alongside newer custom-built homes, with townhouses and low-rise condos in between.

Compare the pockets

North York: Yonge corridor condos compared with interior bungalow streets
CompareYonge corridor condo (Sheppard-Yonge, North York Centre, Finch)Interior bungalow or rebuild (a few blocks off Yonge)
What you're buyingA unit in a building, plus a share of the common elementsLand and a house. On many streets the lot is most of the value
Monthly carrying costProperty tax plus condo fees. Fees follow the corporation's budget, so reserve fund health mattersProperty tax plus your own upkeep, with no monthly fee
Closing costsOntario and Toronto land transfer tax, plus a lawyer's review of the status certificateOntario and Toronto land transfer tax, plus survey, title and inspection costs
Getting aroundWalk to Line 1 (Line 4 from Sheppard-Yonge)Bus to the subway, or drive to Highway 401 and the Don Valley Parkway
Check firstStatus certificate: reserve fund, special assessments, rental ratio, fee historyZoning, lot size and permits if you plan to renovate, add a unit or rebuild
Competing withOther units in the same building, so pricing is relativeFamilies and builders, so the lot can set the price
Investor angleRent against fees. Check the building's rental rules firstOnly count extra units that zoning and permits actually allow

Both sides of this comparison pay the same land transfer tax, since both are in the City of Toronto.

Getting around

  • Line 1 Yonge–University: North York Centre, Sheppard-Yonge and Finch stations
  • Line 4 Sheppard east from Sheppard-Yonge
  • Highway 401 and the Don Valley Parkway nearby

Lifestyle & amenities

Yonge Street has a wide mix of restaurants and shops, including many Persian businesses north of Sheppard. Mel Lastman Square hosts community events, and Yorkdale and Fairview are a short drive away.

  • Mel Lastman Square and North York Civic Centre
  • Earl Bales Park and the West Don trails
  • North York Central Library
  • Yorkdale and Fairview shopping centres

Buyer, seller, investor

BuyingHow buying works →
  • Condo supply is high; compare against other units in the same building
  • On bungalow streets you may be paying for the land; price it as a rebuild lot
SellingHow selling works →
  • In a condo, your competition is the same building, so pricing and presentation decide it
  • Houses on larger lots draw builders as well as families
  • Walking distance to a subway station is a real selling point; lead with it
InvestingHow analysis works →
  • Model the monthly carrying cost first; building fees and rental rules set the income
  • On low-density streets, count only the additional units zoning allows

Before you offer

The questions I ask before any offer here. They're things to confirm, not predictions.

  • Condo status certificate. Read the status certificate and reserve fund study; check monthly fees and the rental ratio.
  • Zoning and rebuilds. Confirm with the City what the lot allows (rebuild, additional units) before pricing it in.
  • Second suites and divided homes. Confirm the unit is registered or legal with the city before counting its rent.

School boundaries change and vary street by street. Confirm them with the board (TDSB, TCDSB) for the exact address.
